sections.title: Critical failure screen and error reporting
sections.what: When the whole app layout fails, sends the error to Sentry and shows a 'Critical System Failure' page with a 'Restart Maate' button. The button calls the reset function so the app can try to load again.
sections.why: Gives users a clear way to recover and makes sure the engineering team hears about the failure.
sections.watch_out: The footer text says 'Production Environment' in fixed text, so it will be wrong in test or staging builds.

summary: A last-resort error screen that appears when the whole app layout fails, and it reports the error to Sentry.
purpose: Shows a 'Critical System Failure' page with a restart button when even the main layout cannot load.
why: Because the normal layout is broken in this case, this screen has to draw its own page structure and cannot rely on the usual layout.
how: When the screen appears, it sends the error to Sentry. It then shows a warning icon, a short explanation, and a restart button that calls the reset function to try again.
inputs: The error object (with an optional digest code) and a reset function supplied by Next.js.
outputs: A full-page error message with a restart button. The error is also sent to Sentry.
risks: The page writes its own html and body tags, so it must not be nested inside another layout. If Sentry is not set up, errors may not be recorded at all.
debug: If users see a blank or plain page after a crash, check that Sentry is configured and that this file still exports a default component. Compare the behavior with error.tsx, which handles smaller page failures.
